question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one JSON-RPC tools/call of resolve-library-id with both required arguments, libraryName Astro and query 'content collections', no Authorization header, no session id, no prior initialize

headers.www-authenticate: a challenge of scheme Bearer naming a resource_metadata document, sent on this 200 (the literal header is in the artifact)

decoded.body: a ranked list of five Astro library ids with snippet counts, source reputation and benchmark scores: the tool ran in full for a caller with no account
decoded.no-ratelimit-headers-here: this response carries NO ratelimit-limit, ratelimit-remaining, ratelimit-reset or context7-quota-tier header. Every keyless REST response carries all four.
decoded.it-draws-on-the-rest-counter: bracketing the call with keyless REST reads of ratelimit-remaining, each of which is itself one request and steps the counter by one: three baseline reads gave 84, 83, 82, then THIS call, then a read of 80. A step of two across one REST read means the tools/call consumed one unit of the same counter.
decoded.a-failed-call-is-free: the same bracket around a tools/call that fails argument validation (libraryName omitted, the server answering 'Input validation error') gave 80 then 79, a step of one: the failed call consumed nothing.
decoded.the-bracket-reads-are-separate-requests: the five REST reads named above are requests of their own, not this one. They are printed in section 8 of the artifact, and the surface, status and command fields here describe only the single MCP POST.
decoded.not-measured: whether an MCP initialize, tools/list, or a query-docs call consume units was not isolated by a bracket of its own, and no 429 was provoked on either surface.

finding: A keyless MCP tools/call of resolve-library-id answers 200 with a real ranked result, and it silently spends the same anonymous allowance the REST API reports. Bracketed by keyless REST reads that each step the counter by one, a successful tools/call produces a step of two (84, 83, 82, then the call, then 80) and a call that fails argument validation produces a step of one (80 then 79). The MCP response itself carries no ratelimit or quota header of any kind. An agent working only over MCP is therefore drawing down a monthly budget that its own surface never shows it, and no vendor page read on this date says the two surfaces share one counter.

reproducibility.command: R(){ curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -m 20 'https://context7.com/api/v2/libs/search?query=astro' | grep -i ratelimit-remaining; }; R; R; R; curl -sS -m 30 -X POST https://mcp.context7.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"resolve-library-id","arguments":{"libraryName":"Astro","query":"content collections"}}}' | head -c 120; R
